text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Kenyan government declares 7.1 million bags of maize and 2.7 million of beans are required to contain famine in the country.
- President Daniel arap Moi directs that the ruling Kenya African National Union party hold grassroots elections in five districts to end leadership wrangles.
- A group of 20 armed bandits shoot dead a police officer in the Mount Kenya area.
- President Moi rules out any extra time for those who fail to acquire the new-generation identity cards by the January 31 deadline.
- A Kisumu court hears how a chief inspector of police raped a 12-year-old girl in his house after removing her from the cells on the pretext he was taking her home to her parents.
- More than 5,000 people in the Rift valley are living in abject poverty after being displaced by cattle rustlers and bandits.
- National Heritage Minister William ole Ntimama says the cabinet is intact and united contrary to malicious rumours circulating that ministers have divided into camps.
- The president scraps examination fees and building fund fees charged to the parents of primary schoolchildren. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
